question: In which season do the dry and hot winds known as 'Loo' blow in the afternoon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Hot Weather Season**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Loo wind:__

 
• The Loo is a strong, dry and hot afternoon wind from the west in the summer, blowing over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India and Pakistan.
 
• It is particularly strong in the months of May and June.
 
• Exposure to it also leads to lethal heat strokes because of its extremely high temperatures (45 °C–50 °C or 115 °F-120 °F).
 
• The technical words that signify the direction in which the wind is blowing are 'Windward' and 'leeward.'
 
• The direction upwind from the point of reference is windward.
 
• Loo has extended its reach and has now gripped more parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and even West Madhya Pradesh. Moreover, some parts of this region are also reeling under heat wave conditions.
